To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bacterial flora of the ACF is a mixture of bacteria that are also found on the hands and arms, and the forehead.
the surface bacterial flora of the ACF of most subjects is readily eliminated by alcohol disinfectant and that in some subjects a small surviving population persists.

alcohol disinfection is more effective against the ACF flora of some persons than of others, that the flora of the palm is more susceptible to alcohol than the ACF flora, that the ACF flora is more susceptible to the alcohol than the forehead flora, and that the ACF is a good site for the study of the efficacy of alcohol in the treatment of skin flora because of the presence of alcohol resistant bacteria on many persons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surface flora of the ACF, palm and forehead.
the bacterial flora on the skin, and with the effects of alcohol disinfection on the surface and subsurface bacterial flora.
the bacterial flora of the skin, particularly the antecubitial fossae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the flora of the anteeubital fossa is the same as that of the skin of the hands, back and face; 2) the flora of these areas is bimodal; 3) alcohol disinfection is highly effective in reducing the population densities of all bacteria except P. acnes, P. saccharolytic, S. ep. and an aerobic diph.
alcohol disinfection of the ACF is effective against most bacteria but not all.
alcohol disinfection is not effective in eliminating all bacteria from the antecubitally exposed areas of the skin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alcohol disinfection of the skin is not as effective as previously believed, that the efficacy depends on the initial surface flora, that there is a correlation of the surviving population on the ACF with the surface flora, and that there is a relationship between the surviving population and the species of bacteria present in the initial survey.
the ACF flora is similar to that of the hand and back, and that alcohol disinfection eliminates the ACF flora of most subjects, but not of those with the most abundant flora.
the surface flora of the palm and ACF is transient but the subsurface flora of the ACF and the forehead is sheltered and resistant to alcohol disinfection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alcohol disinfection of the ACF is not a reliable way to eliminate bacteria from the skin surface.
the ACF is not an appropriate site for the study of skin flora because it is so readily and effectively disinfectible.
the ACF is a site where bacteria can be protected from alcohol disinfection and that this protection can persist for a long time.
